# RichText

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Lays out styled text spans with wrapping and pagination.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`. Extends `ElementBase`. Implements `IStatefulElement`, `IRoleProvider`.

## Constructors

```typescript
new RichText(options?: RichTextOptions)
```

## Properties

- [`alignment`](#alignment): Paragraph alignment.
- [`defaultStyle`](#defaultstyle): Default style inherited by all spans.
- [`minLinesAfterBreak`](#minlinesafterbreak): Minimum number of lines that must appear after a page break (widow control).
- [`minLinesBeforeBreak`](#minlinesbeforebreak): Minimum number of lines to render before a page break (orphan control).
- [`semanticRole`](#semanticrole): RichText renders one flowing paragraph, so it tags as /P.

### `alignment`

```typescript
alignment: TextAlignment
```

Paragraph alignment. Accepts `'left' | 'center' | 'right' | 'middle' | 'justify'`. When not set explicitly, an enclosing Container whose horizontalAlignment is Start/Center/End supplies an ambient default instead of the plain Left below; see `effectiveAlignment`.

Example, from `code-recipes/text-styling/rich-text-styles`:

```typescript
rt6.alignment = TextAlignment.Justify;
```

Example, from `code-recipes/text-styling/rich-text-styles`:

```typescript
rt7.alignment = TextAlignment.Justify;
```

### `defaultStyle`

```typescript
defaultStyle: TextStyle
```

Default style inherited by all spans. Span-level styles override these values.

Example, from `code-recipes/text-styling/rich-text-styles`:

```typescript
rt7.defaultStyle = disclaimerBase;
```

Example, from `code-recipes/links-references/hyperlinks`:

```typescript
sentence.defaultStyle = new TextStyle().withFamily('Helvetica').withSize(11).withColor(ColorPalette.slate[600]);
```

### `minLinesAfterBreak`

```typescript
minLinesAfterBreak: number
```

Minimum number of lines that must appear after a page break (widow control).

### `minLinesBeforeBreak`

```typescript
minLinesBeforeBreak: number
```

Minimum number of lines to render before a page break (orphan control).

### `semanticRole`

```typescript
readonly semanticRole: SemanticRole
```

*read-only*

RichText renders one flowing paragraph, so it tags as /P. Without a role the pipeline would emit its text as untagged content (PDF/UA 7.1).

### `line`

```typescript

```

Adds a text span followed by a line break.

### `lineBreak`

```typescript
lineBreak(): RichText
```

Adds a line break (empty line).

### `link`

```typescript
link(text: string, uri: string, style?: TextStyle | ((style: TextStyle) => void)): RichText
```

Adds a span that links to a URI, in the flow of the paragraph.

The span's style is its look (a colour, an underline); the link adds only the clickable region, one per line the span wraps onto, and tags it as a Link for screen readers.

Example:

```typescript
new RichText()
  .span('Read our ')
  .link('terms of service', 'https://example.com/terms', s => s.withColor('blue-700').underline())
  .span(' before you order.');
```

### `renderStateful`

```typescript
renderStateful(ctx: RenderContext, width: number): RenderStatus
```

Renders this element with state tracking for pagination. Unlike Render(), this method returns a status indicating whether more content needs to be rendered on subsequent pages.

- `ctx`: The render context
- `width`: The available width for this element

### `resetState`

```typescript
resetState(): void
```

Resets the internal state of this element, preparing it for a fresh render. Should be called before starting a new document or after completing a multipage render.

### `span`

```typescript
span(text: string, style?: TextStyle | ((style: TextStyle) => void)): RichText
```

Adds a text span.

- `text`: - The span's text
- `style`: - A style, or a callback that configures a fresh one

Example:

```typescript
const rich = new RichText();
rich.span('Payment due within ');
rich.span('30 days', new TextStyle().bold());
rich.span(' of the invoice date, or ', s => s.underline());
```
